title: MLE, MAP and the bootstrap

wrong.mle_unbiased_variance.py: gaussian_mle divides by n-1 (ddof=1), which is the unbiased estimator, not the maximum-likelihood one
wrong.nll_missing_log_sigma.py: gaussian_nll drops the n*log(sigma) term, so the minimum over sigma is at infinity
wrong.nll_sigma_squared.py: gaussian_nll treats sigma as a variance (divides by sigma, not sigma squared)
wrong.map_uses_mean.py: bernoulli_map returns the posterior mean (k+a)/(n+a+b) instead of the mode
wrong.map_forgets_minus_one.py: bernoulli_map uses (k+a)/(n+a+b-2): off by one in the numerator
wrong.bootstrap_resamples_rows.py: bootstrap_means averages the index array instead of the resampled data
wrong.ci_wrong_tail.py: percentile_ci uses alpha instead of alpha/2 in each tail
wrong.ci_sorted_in_place.py: percentile_ci sorts the caller's array in place

hints: Gaussian MLE: setting the derivative of the log-likelihood to zero gives the sample mean and the variance with divisor n (not n-1). The NLL is n*log(sigma) + sum((x-mu)^2)/(2 sigma^2) + n/2 * log(2 pi).
Bernoulli with a Beta(a, b) prior: the posterior is Beta(k + a, n - k + b). Its mode, the MAP estimate, is (k + a - 1) / (n + a + b - 2).

Bootstrap: idx is a (B, n) array of row indices, so x[idx] is (B, n) and the mean over axis 1 gives B resampled means. For a (1 - alpha) interval take the alpha/2 and 1 - alpha/2 percentiles; np.percentile does not need a pre-sorted array, so do not sort the caller's data.
